ecological_hypothesis: Duration of simultaneous hot and fresh conditions contains plant-condition information beyond the durations of hot and fresh stress considered separately.
exposure_source: Exact published Beck et al. 2024 GAM-derived daily reconstruction pinned by results/compound_hotfresh_v1_contract.json.

exposure_mapping.hot_feature: segment mean station-level maximum run of temperature >= 30 C
exposure_mapping.fresh_feature: segment mean station-level maximum run of salinity <= 25 ppt
exposure_mapping.compound_feature: segment mean station-level maximum run with both simultaneously true

validation.split: strict walk-forward by target year; train only on earlier target years

support_rule.overall_primary_support: At least one of the two primary outcomes passes the full win/median rule and p<0.025; report the other primary outcome regardless.

interpretation.positive: Joint hot-fresh duration carries outcome-specific information beyond hot and fresh durations separately, consistent with a compound-stress candidate mechanism.
interpretation.negative: The published joint-duration metric does not explain fixed-transect Thalassia condition beyond local legacy plus marginal hot/fresh stress; compound climate stress may operate at finer spatial/temporal or physiological scales.

claim_boundary: Retrospective ecological test using published model-derived exposure; not prospective climate prediction.
The threshold metrics are stress indices, not proven species-specific physiological boundaries.
Segment-level exposure is spatially coarser than the fixed transect response.
A positive result is association/predictive evidence for a compound-stress candidate, not causal identification.
Do not alter thresholds, exposure aggregation, outcomes, baseline, years or familywise rule after opening focal responses.
